<p>中心原子周围的<b>价层电子对</b>（成键电子对与孤对电子）带负电，彼此:
The valence electron pairs around a central atom (bonding pairs and lone pairs) are negatively charged, so they repel one another and move as far apart as possible.

On the left, every electron domain is pushed across a sphere by all the others. Add or remove pairs, or click Shake, and watch them spring apart into the most stable arrangement.

A lone pair is held by only one nucleus, so it sits closer to it and spreads wider. That makes its repulsion stronger.
<p>CH₄、NH₃、H₂O 的中心原子都有 <b>4 对</b>价层电子，电子:
The central atoms of CH₄, NH₃ and H₂O all have 4 pairs of valence electrons, so all three have a tetrahedral electron geometry (the green polyhedron).

Molecular geometry counts only the atoms. A lone pair occupies a vertex but is “invisible”, so NH₃ is trigonal pyramidal and H₂O is bent.
<p>排斥强弱：<b>孤对–孤对 &gt; 孤对–成键 &gt; 成键–成键</:
Repulsion strength: lone–lone > lone–bond > bond–bond.

The more lone pairs, the closer the bonding pairs are squeezed and the smaller the bond angle:

CH₄ 109.5° > NH₃ 107° > H₂O 104.5°

The arcs are labelled with measured bond angles. The shapes come from the repulsion model, which follows the same trend as experiment.
<p>中心原子用能量相近的原子轨道“混合”出数目相同、能量相等的<b>杂化轨道<:
The central atom “mixes” atomic orbitals of similar energy into the same number of equivalent hybrid orbitals. Each hybrid orbital holds one electron domain.

Number of hybrid orbitals = number of valence electron pairs: 2 → sp, 3 → sp², 4 → sp³, 5 → sp³d, 6 → sp³d².

In ethylene, acetylene and benzene, the unhybridized p orbitals form π bonds.
<p>每个极性键都有一个<b>键偶极</b>（细箭头，指向电负性大的一端）。</:
Every polar bond has a bond dipole (thin arrow, pointing to the more electronegative end).

Add them as vectors. If the net dipole is zero the molecule is nonpolar; otherwise it is polar (thick arrow μ).

Both have three atoms: linear CO₂ cancels its dipoles, while bent SO₂ does not.
<p>第三周期及以后的元素可以有 5、6 甚至 7 个电子域。</p><p>三角:
Elements from period 3 onward can have 5, 6 or even 7 electron domains.

In a trigonal bipyramid an equatorial site has only two 90° neighbours while an axial site has three, so lone pairs fill equatorial sites first: SF₄ is a seesaw, ClF₃ is T-shaped and XeF₂ is linear.

In an octahedron two lone pairs sit trans to each other, so XeF₄ is square planar.
<p>碳原子连着四个<b>互不相同</b>的原子或基团时，分子与它的镜像就像左右:
When a carbon atom carries four different atoms or groups, the molecule and its mirror image are like left and right hands: no rotation can superimpose them.

Click Superimpose to turn the mirror image onto the original and see which atoms fail to match.
<p>按 VSEPR 类型浏览全部分子。拖动旋转，滚轮缩放。</p>: Browse every molecule by VSEPR class. Drag to rotate and scroll to zoom.
两个 C=O 键偶极大小相等、方向相反，相互抵消，所以 CO₂ 是非极性分子。: The two C=O bond dipoles are equal and opposite, so they cancel and CO₂ is nonpolar.
Be 只有 2 对价层电子，相距最远的排布是直线。: Be has only 2 valence electron pairs. The farthest-apart arrangement is a straight line.
三键在 VSEPR 中只算一个电子域，因此 C 周围只有 2 个电子域。: A triple bond counts as a single electron domain in VSEPR, so C has only 2 domains.
B 只有 3 对价层电子，三个 F 在同一平面上互成 120°。: B has only 3 valence electron pairs. The three F atoms lie in one plane, 120° apart.
双键电子密度更大，把两个 C–H 键挤得更近，H–C–H 只有 116.5°。: The double bond carries more electron density and squeezes the two C–H bonds together, so H–C–H is only 116.5°.
S 上有一对孤对电子，分子呈 V 形，键偶极不能抵消。: S carries one lone pair, so the molecule is bent and the bond dipoles do not cancel.
三个原子都是氧，但中心 O 与端位 O 的电子环境不同，臭氧有微弱极性。: All three atoms are oxygen, but the central O and the terminal O atoms have different electron environments, so ozone is slightly polar.
4 对成键电子指向正四面体的四个顶点，键角 109°28′。: Four bonding pairs point to the four vertices of a tetrahedron, with bond angles of 109°28′.
NH₃ 的孤对电子与 H⁺ 形成配位键，四个 N–H 完全等同。: The lone pair of NH₃ forms a coordinate bond with H⁺, making all four N–H bonds identical.
C–Cl 键有极性，但正四面体对称使合偶极为零。: Each C–Cl bond is polar, but tetrahedral symmetry makes the net dipole zero.
把 CCl₄ 的一个 Cl 换成 H，对称性被破坏，分子变为极性。: Replacing one Cl of CCl₄ with H breaks the symmetry, so the molecule becomes polar.
一对孤对电子占据四面体的一个顶点，排斥更强，把键角压到 107°。: One lone pair occupies a vertex of the tetrahedron. Its stronger repulsion squeezes the bond angle to 107°.
两对孤对电子进一步挤压成键电子对，键角只有 104.5°。: Two lone pairs squeeze the bonding pairs even further, so the bond angle is only 104.5°.
轴向与赤道位不等价：轴向 P–Cl 键（214 pm）比赤道位（202 pm）更: Axial and equatorial sites are not equivalent: the axial P–Cl bonds (214 pm) are longer than the equatorial ones (202 pm).
孤对电子占赤道位，那里只有两个 90° 邻居，排斥最小。: The lone pair takes an equatorial site, which has only two 90° neighbours and the least repulsion.
两对孤对电子都在赤道位，剩下三个 F 呈 T 形。: Both lone pairs take equatorial sites, leaving the three F atoms in a T shape.
三对孤对电子占满赤道平面，两个 F 只能在轴向，分子是直线形。: Three lone pairs fill the equatorial plane, so the two F atoms must be axial and the molecule is linear.
与 XeF₂ 同为 AX₂E₃，直线形。: Like XeF₂ it is AX₂E₃, and linear.
6 对成键电子指向正八面体的六个顶点。: Six bonding pairs point to the six vertices of an octahedron.
孤对电子把四个底面 F 推向另一侧，四方锥略呈“伞”形。: The lone pair pushes the four basal F atoms away, so the square pyramid looks slightly like an umbrella.
两对孤对电子取反式位置彼此最远，四个 F 共平面。: The two lone pairs sit trans, as far apart as possible, and the four F atoms are coplanar.
7 个电子域：赤道面上 5 个 F 互成 72°，两个轴向 F 在上下。: Seven electron domains: five equatorial F atoms 72° apart, with two axial F atoms above and below.
碳连着四个不同的原子，它与镜像无法重合，是最简单的手性分子之一。: The carbon carries four different atoms, so the molecule cannot be superimposed on its mirror image. It is one of the simplest chiral molecules.
每个 C 为 sp² 杂化，未参与杂化的 p 轨道肩并肩重叠形成 π 键，六个原: Each C is sp² hybridized. The unhybridized p orbitals overlap side by side to form a π bond, and all six atoms are coplanar.
每个 C 为 sp 杂化，两套 p 轨道形成两个互相垂直的 π 键，分子是直线形: Each C is sp hybridized. Two sets of p orbitals form two perpendicular π bonds, and the molecule is linear.
六个 C 均为 sp² 杂化，六个 p 轨道形成环状离域大 π 键，六条 C–C: All six C atoms are sp² hybridized. Their six p orbitals form a delocalized ring of π electrons, and all six C–C bonds are identical.
中间的碳连着 H、OH、CH₃、COOH 四个不同基团，是手性碳；L-乳酸与 D: The middle carbon carries four different groups, H, OH, CH₃ and COOH, so it is a chiral carbon. L- and D-lactic acid are mirror images.
电子对相互排斥，正在寻找平衡…: Pairs repel each other, searching for balance…
困在局部极小，施加热扰动: Stuck in a local minimum, applying a thermal kick
旋转后总有两个基团位置互换——无法重合: After any rotation two groups are swapped, so they cannot be superimposed

<p>我们无法同时确定电子的位置和速度，只能说电子<b>在某处出现的概率</b>:
We cannot pin down an electron's position and velocity at the same time. We can only say how likely it is to be found in a given place.

Each dot on the stage is one electron position recorded by a “measurement”. The more we record, the more clearly the density of dots reveals the probability density |ψ|². That is the electron cloud.

Dense regions are where the electron is most likely to be found, not places with many electrons.
能级与构造原理: Energy levels and the Aufbau principle
<p>多电子原子中，电子按以下规则逐个填入轨道：</p><p><b>能量最低原理:
In a many-electron atom, electrons fill orbitals one by one following these rules:

Aufbau principle: lower energy levels fill first. Note that 4s fills before 3d.

Pauli principle: an orbital holds at most 2 electrons, with opposite spins.

Hund's rule: within one level, electrons first occupy separate orbitals with parallel spins.
<p>三个量子数确定一个原子轨道：</p><p><b>n</b> 主量子数，决定:
Three quantum numbers identify an atomic orbital:

n, the principal quantum number, sets the shell and size; l, the angular quantum number (0 ≤ l ≤ n − 1), sets the shape; m, the magnetic quantum number (−l ≤ m ≤ l), sets the orientation.

Total nodes = n − 1: l angular nodes and n − l − 1 radial nodes.
<p>1s 到 4f 的全部 30 个原子轨道。拖动旋转，滚轮缩放。</p>: All 30 atomic orbitals from 1s to 4f. Drag to rotate and scroll to zoom.
s 轨道球形对称，没有角节面。: s orbitals are spherically symmetric and have no angular nodes.
p 轨道呈哑铃形，两瓣相位相反，中间隔着一个节平面。: p orbitals are dumbbells: two lobes of opposite phase separated by a nodal plane.
d 轨道多为四叶花瓣形，有两个角节面；dz² 的两个角节面是圆锥面。: Most d orbitals are four-leaf clovers with two angular nodes; for dz² the two angular nodes are cones.
f 轨道有三个角节面，形状更复杂。: f orbitals have three angular nodes and more complex shapes.
径向分布 · {0} 的峰值在 r ≈ {1} a₀: Radial distribution · {0} peaks at r ≈ {1} a₀
特例：3d 半充满（d⁵）或全充满（d¹⁰）时能量更低，于是从 4s 借来一个电: Exception: a half-filled (d⁵) or full (d¹⁰) 3d subshell is lower in energy, so one electron is borrowed from 4s. The Aufbau principle alone would give {0}.
<b>泡利原理</b>：{0} 的这个轨道已有一个电子，新电子与它自旋相反、配成: Pauli principle: this {0} orbital already holds one electron, so the new electron pairs with it with opposite spin.
<b>洪特规则</b>：{0} 还有空轨道，新电子先单独占据，自旋与前面的电子平: Hund's rule: {0} still has an empty orbital, so the new electron occupies it alone, with spin parallel to the others.
<b>能量最低原理</b>：更低的能级已填满，电子进入下一个能级 {0}。: Aufbau principle: the lower levels are full, so the electron enters the next level, {0}.
<br>4s 的能量比 3d 低，所以先填 4s。: 4s is lower in energy than 3d, so 4s fills first.
三个 2p 轨道能量相同，分别沿 x、y、z 轴伸展，互相垂直。合在一起时电子云: The three 2p orbitals have the same energy and point along x, y and z, perpendicular to one another. Together their electron cloud is spherically symmetric.

<p>分子不停地运动、碰撞，但<b>绝大多数碰撞并不发生反应</b>（灰色微光）:
Molecules move and collide constantly, yet almost no collisions lead to reaction (faint grey sparks).

Only a collision that meets two conditions is an effective collision (golden flash):

① the energy along the line of impact ≥ the activation energy Ea; ② the orientation is right: H₂ and I₂ must meet side by side to break the old bonds and form two H–I bonds at once.
<p>同一温度下，分子的能量并不相同，而是服从<b>麦克斯韦–玻尔兹曼分布</b:
At one temperature, molecules do not all share the same energy; they follow the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution (white curve).

Molecules with energy ≥ Ea are activated molecules; they glow orange on the stage.

Raise the temperature and the curve flattens and widens: the fraction of activated molecules rises sharply, and so do effective collisions. That is why reactions speed up when heated.
<p>底部的铂表面是<b>催化剂</b>。分子吸附在表面上，旧键被削弱、取向被摆:
The platinum surface at the bottom is a catalyst. Molecules adsorbed on it have weakened bonds and aligned orientations, so the reaction takes a path with lower activation energy (green dashed line).

At the same temperature, more collisions clear the lower barrier: green flashes cluster on the catalyst surface.

A catalyst does not change ΔH, and it is itself unchanged by the reaction.
<p>单位体积内的分子越多，单位时间内的碰撞次数越多，有效碰撞也就越多。</p>:
The more molecules per unit volume, the more collisions per unit time, and the more effective collisions.

Push the piston to compress the gas, or add reactants, and watch the collision frequency and reaction rate change.

Note: the fraction of activated molecules is unchanged; what changes is their number per unit volume.
<p>2NO₂（红棕色）⇌ N₂O₄（无色）。</p><p>开始时只有 NO₂，:
2NO₂ (red-brown) ⇌ N₂O₄ (colourless).

At first there is only NO₂: the forward reaction is fast and the reverse slow. As N₂O₄ builds up, the reverse reaction speeds up.

When the forward rate = reverse rate, concentrations stop changing and chemical equilibrium is reached. At the molecular level both reactions never stop: this is a dynamic equilibrium.

Starting from NO₂ or from N₂O₄, the system reaches the same equilibrium.
<p>改变条件，平衡会向<b>减弱这种改变</b>的方向移动（勒夏特列原理）。<:
When conditions change, equilibrium shifts in the direction that counteracts the change (Le Chatelier's principle).

Heating: shifts toward the endothermic direction (more NO₂), so the colour darkens.

Compression: shifts toward fewer gas molecules (more N₂O₄). Look closely: the colour first darkens (higher concentration), then lightens a little.
<p>H₂ 与 Cl₂ 混合，在暗处几乎不反应；一旦<b>强光照射</b>就会爆:
A mixture of H₂ and Cl₂ barely reacts in the dark, but explodes under strong light.

Light splits Cl₂ into two chlorine atoms Cl· (radicals, the glowing spheres). Each Cl· takes an H from H₂, forming HCl and H·; the H· takes a Cl from Cl₂, regenerating Cl·…

One radical can trigger thousands of reactions while releasing a lot of heat, so the reaction accelerates. This is a chain reaction.

化学反应微观演示：有效碰撞与取向、麦克斯韦–玻尔兹曼分布与活化分子、催化剂表面、: Microscopic views of chemical reactions: effective collisions and orientation, the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution and activated molecules, catalyst surfaces, concentration and pressure, reaching and shifting equilibrium, and a light-triggered chain explosion.
速率 = k[CH₃Br][OH⁻]，二级反应。手性碳发生构型翻转（瓦尔登翻转）: Rate = k[CH₃Br][OH⁻], second order. A chiral carbon inverts its configuration (Walden inversion), like an umbrella flipped inside out by the wind.
C–Br 键极性很强，碳带部分正电荷。三个 H 像一把伞，伞面朝向左边。: The C–Br bond is strongly polar, leaving carbon partially positive. The three H atoms form an umbrella opening to the left.
OH⁻ 从溴的背面（180°）进攻碳原子：一对孤对电子指向碳，C–Br 键的电子: OH⁻ attacks carbon from the side opposite bromine (180°): a lone pair points at carbon while the C–Br electrons shift toward bromine.
五配位过渡态：O···C···Br 共线，三个 H 处在同一平面上，像伞被吹到水: A five-coordinate transition state: O···C···Br are collinear and the three H atoms lie in one plane, like an umbrella blown flat. The new and old bonds are each only “half” formed.
C–O 键形成，Br⁻ 离开。三个 H 翻到右边——构型发生了翻转。: The C–O bond forms and Br⁻ leaves. The three H atoms flip to the right: the configuration has inverted.
速率 = k[(CH₃)₃CBr]，一级反应，只与底物有关。碳正离子是平面的，亲: Rate = k[(CH₃)₃CBr], first order, depending only on the substrate. The carbocation is planar, so the nucleophile can attack from either face and a chiral substrate racemises.
中心碳连着三个甲基和一个溴，背面被甲基挡住，SN2 很难发生。: The central carbon carries three methyl groups and a bromine. The methyls block the back side, so SN2 is very difficult.
C–Br 键自发异裂，溴带着一对电子离开——这是决定速率的一步。: The C–Br bond breaks heterolytically and bromine leaves with the electron pair. This is the rate-determining step.
生成平面三角形的叔丁基碳正离子，三个甲基的推电子作用使它比较稳定。: A trigonal planar tert-butyl carbocation forms, stabilised by electron donation from the three methyl groups.
水分子的孤对电子进攻碳正离子——它可以从平面的上方或下方进攻。: A lone pair on water attacks the carbocation, from either above or below the plane.
另一个水分子夺走质子，得到叔丁醇和 H₃O⁺。: Another water molecule removes the proton, giving tert-butanol and H₃O⁺.
H₃O⁺ 与 Br⁻ 在溶液中相当于氢溴酸（这里画成 HBr 分子）。: H₃O⁺ and Br⁻ in solution amount to hydrobromic acid (drawn here as an HBr molecule).
一步协同。被夺去的 β-H 与离去的 Br 必须处在反式共平面（二面角 180°: One concerted step. The β-H being removed and the leaving Br must be anti-periplanar (dihedral angle 180°). The product is an alkene.
旋转到 β-H 与 Br 处于反式共平面的构象：一个朝上，一个朝下。: The molecule rotates into the conformation where β-H and Br are anti-periplanar: one points up, the other down.
OH⁻ 夺取 β-H；C–H 键的电子转移形成 π 键；C–Br 键的电子随 B: OH⁻ removes β-H; the C–H electrons move to form the π bond; the C–Br electrons leave with Br⁻. All three happen at once.
O···H···C 与 C···Br 同时部分成键、部分断键，C–C 键获得部分: O···H···C and C···Br are simultaneously part-formed and part-broken, and the C–C bond gains partial double-bond character.
形成 C=C 双键，同时生成水和 Br⁻。: The C=C double bond forms, along with water and Br⁻.
费歇尔酯化：加成–消除机理，经过四面体中间体。H⁺ 在第一步被消耗、最后一步再生: Fischer esterification: an addition–elimination mechanism through a tetrahedral intermediate. H⁺ is used in the first step and regenerated in the last, so it is a catalyst.
乙酸、¹⁸O 标记的乙醇和催化剂 H₃O⁺。: Acetic acid, ¹⁸O-labelled ethanol and the catalyst H₃O⁺.
羰基氧接受 H⁺，羰基碳的正电性大大增强，更容易被弱亲核试剂进攻。: The carbonyl oxygen accepts H⁺, making the carbonyl carbon much more positive and easier for a weak nucleophile to attack.
乙醇的 ¹⁸O 进攻羰基碳，生成四面体中间体。: The ¹⁸O of ethanol attacks the carbonyl carbon, forming a tetrahedral intermediate.
质子从 ¹⁸O 转移到原羧基的 –OH 上，把它变成好的离去基团 –OH₂⁺。: A proton moves from ¹⁸O to the original –OH of the acid, turning it into the good leaving group –OH₂⁺.
C=O 重新形成，一分子水离开。注意：离开的水中的氧来自乙酸。: C=O re-forms and a water molecule leaves. Note that the oxygen in this water comes from the acid.
水分子夺回 H⁺，得到乙酸乙酯，H₃O⁺ 再生。整个过程每一步都可逆。: Water takes back H⁺, giving ethyl acetate and regenerating H₃O⁺. Every step of the process is reversible.
滴有酚酞的 NaOH 溶液中逐滴加入盐酸，红色恰好褪去时酸碱恰好中和。Na⁺ 和: Add hydrochloric acid drop by drop to NaOH solution containing phenolphthalein; when the pink just disappears, the acid and base exactly neutralise. Na⁺ and Cl⁻ take no part.
酸溶液中的 H⁺ 实际以水合氢离子 H₃O⁺ 的形式存在；碱溶液中有 OH⁻。: H⁺ in acid solution actually exists as the hydronium ion H₃O⁺; base solution contains OH⁻.
带正电的 H₃O⁺ 与带负电的 OH⁻ 相互吸引、靠近。: Positive H₃O⁺ and negative OH⁻ attract and approach each other.
H⁺ 从 H₃O⁺ 转移到 OH⁻ 上，生成两个水分子，并放出热量（中和热）。: H⁺ passes from H₃O⁺ to OH⁻, forming two water molecules and releasing heat (heat of neutralisation).
立即产生白色沉淀，加稀硝酸沉淀不溶解。常用来检验 Cl⁻。Na⁺ 和 NO₃⁻: A white precipitate forms at once and does not dissolve in dilute nitric acid. This is a common test for Cl⁻. Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ are spectator ions.
AgNO₃ 和 NaCl 都完全电离，溶液中有 Ag⁺、NO₃⁻、Na⁺、Cl⁻: AgNO₃ and NaCl are fully dissociated, so four kinds of ions move freely: Ag⁺, NO₃⁻, Na⁺ and Cl⁻.
Ag⁺ 与 Cl⁻ 相互吸引，按一正一负交替排列，开始形成晶核。: Ag⁺ and Cl⁻ attract each other and line up in alternating positive and negative positions, starting a crystal nucleus.
越来越多的离子加入，晶体长大到肉眼可见，沉降为白色的 AgCl。Na⁺、NO₃⁻: More and more ions join until the crystal is visible and settles as white AgCl. Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ stay in solution throughout, so the ionic equation includes only the ions that actually react.
锌片表面析出红色的铜，溶液蓝色逐渐变浅。本质是电子从 Zn 转移到 Cu²⁺。: Red copper deposits on the zinc and the blue solution fades. At heart, electrons move from Zn to Cu²⁺.
左边是锌的金属晶体，溶液中有蓝色的 Cu²⁺（硫酸根未画出）。: On the left is the zinc metal lattice; the solution contains blue Cu²⁺ (sulfate not shown).
Cu²⁺ 移动到锌表面。锌比铜活泼，更容易失去电子。: Cu²⁺ moves to the zinc surface. Zinc is more reactive than copper and loses electrons more easily.
每个锌原子失去 2 个电子变成 Zn²⁺ 进入溶液；Cu²⁺ 得到这 2 个电子: Each zinc atom loses 2 electrons and enters the solution as Zn²⁺; each Cu²⁺ gains those 2 electrons and becomes a copper atom on the zinc surface.
钠浮在水面上，熔成小球，四处游动，发出嘶嘶声；滴入酚酞的溶液变红。: Sodium floats, melts into a ball, darts around and hisses; the solution with phenolphthalein turns pink.
钠是很活泼的金属，最外层只有 1 个电子，很容易失去。: Sodium is a very reactive metal with a single outer electron that it loses easily.
两个钠原子各失去 1 个电子变成 Na⁺；电子被水分子中的 H 获得。: Two sodium atoms each lose 1 electron to become Na⁺; the electrons are taken up by H atoms of water.
两个 H 原子结合成氢气逸出，水分子剩下的部分变成 OH⁻，所以溶液显碱性。反应: Two H atoms join into hydrogen gas, and what remains of each water molecule becomes OH⁻, so the solution is basic. The reaction releases a lot of heat, melting the sodium into a ball.
H₂ 分子离开，留下 Na⁺ 和 OH⁻。: The H₂ molecule leaves, leaving Na⁺ and OH⁻ behind.
饱和碳酸钠溶液液面上出现有香味的油状液体（乙酸乙酯）。浓硫酸作催化剂和吸水剂。: A fragrant oily liquid (ethyl acetate) appears on the saturated sodium carbonate solution. Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as catalyst and dehydrating agent.
乙酸与乙醇。用 ¹⁸O 标记乙醇中的氧原子，看它最后去了哪里。: Acetic acid and ethanol. The oxygen in ethanol is labelled with ¹⁸O so we can see where it ends up.
乙醇的 ¹⁸O 用孤对电子进攻羧基碳；与此同时，羧基上的 –OH 准备离开。: The ¹⁸O of ethanol attacks the carboxyl carbon with a lone pair, while the –OH of the acid prepares to leave.
旧键断裂、新键形成: Old bonds break, new bonds form
C–¹⁸O 键逐渐形成，C–OH 键逐渐断裂；乙醇羟基上的 H 转移到离去的 –: The C–¹⁸O bond forms as the C–OH bond breaks; the H from ethanol's hydroxyl moves to the departing –OH.
¹⁸O 留在乙酸乙酯中，水中的氧来自乙酸——“酸脱羟基，醇脱氢”。: ¹⁸O stays in ethyl acetate, and the oxygen in water comes from the acid: “the acid loses OH, the alcohol loses H”.
油层逐渐消失。碱性条件下水解进行到底；油脂在碱性条件下的水解叫皂化反应，可用来制: The oily layer gradually disappears. Under basic conditions hydrolysis goes to completion; for fats this is called saponification and is used to make soap.
OH⁻ 进攻缺电子的羰基碳，C=O 中的一对电子转移到氧上。: OH⁻ attacks the electron-poor carbonyl carbon and one electron pair of C=O moves onto oxygen.
碳原子暂时连着四个基团，变成四面体构型，羰基氧带负电。: The carbon briefly carries four groups in a tetrahedral arrangement, and the carbonyl oxygen is negatively charged.
C=O 重新形成，乙氧基 CH₃CH₂O⁻ 被挤走。: C=O re-forms and pushes out ethoxide, CH₃CH₂O⁻.
强碱 CH₃CH₂O⁻ 夺走羧酸的质子，生成乙酸根和乙醇。这一步几乎不可逆，所以: The strong base CH₃CH₂O⁻ takes the acid's proton, giving acetate and ethanol. This step is almost irreversible, so base hydrolysis goes to completion.
溴的红棕色迅速褪去。可以用来鉴别乙烯和甲烷。: The red-brown bromine colour fades quickly. This distinguishes ethylene from methane.
乙烯分子中的碳碳双键里有一个容易断裂的 π 键。: The C=C double bond of ethylene contains a π bond that breaks easily.
Br₂ 靠近富含电子的双键，被极化成 Brδ+–Brδ−。: Approaching the electron-rich double bond, Br₂ is polarised into Brδ+–Brδ−.
π 键断开，两个碳同时与一个溴相连，形成三元环溴鎓离子；另一个溴变成 Br⁻。: The π bond breaks and both carbons bond to one bromine, forming a three-membered bromonium ion; the other bromine becomes Br⁻.
Br⁻ 从溴鎓离子的背面进攻碳原子，环打开，得到 1,2-二溴乙烷。两个溴分别加: Br⁻ attacks a carbon from the back of the bromonium ion, opening the ring to give 1,2-dibromoethane. The two bromines add to opposite sides of the former double bond.
得到聚乙烯，一种常见的塑料，可以制成保鲜膜和食品袋。: The product is polyethylene, a common plastic used for cling film and food bags.
许多乙烯分子（单体），每个都含碳碳双键。: Many ethylene molecules (monomers), each with a C=C double bond.
每个双键中的 π 键断开，碳原子上各留下一个未成对电子。: The π bond of each double bond breaks, leaving an unpaired electron on each carbon.
相邻单体之间形成新的 C–C 键，连成长长的碳链——聚乙烯。链节是 –CH₂–C: New C–C bonds form between neighbouring monomers, building a long carbon chain: polyethylene. The repeating unit is –CH₂–CH₂–.
黄绿色逐渐变浅，试管壁出现油状液滴，液面上升。还会继续生成 CH₂Cl₂、CHC: The yellow-green colour fades, oily drops appear on the tube wall and the liquid level rises. CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃ and CCl₄ also form.
甲烷与氯气混合，在暗处不反应。: Methane and chlorine mixed in the dark do not react.
光使 Cl–Cl 键均裂，生成两个带有未成对电子的氯原子 Cl·（自由基）。: Light splits the Cl–Cl bond evenly, giving two chlorine atoms Cl· with unpaired electrons (radicals).
Cl· 从甲烷中夺取一个氢原子，生成 HCl 和甲基自由基 ·CH₃。: Cl· takes a hydrogen atom from methane, forming HCl and the methyl radical ·CH₃.
·CH₃ 呈平面三角形，碳上有一个未成对电子。: ·CH₃ is trigonal planar, with an unpaired electron on carbon.
·CH₃ 夺取 Cl₂ 中的一个氯原子，生成一氯甲烷，同时又产生新的 Cl·，链: ·CH₃ takes one chlorine atom from Cl₂, forming chloromethane and a new Cl·, so the chain continues.
铜丝在火焰上变黑（生成 CuO），插入乙醇后又变红，并闻到刺激性气味（乙醛）。铜: The copper wire turns black in the flame (forming CuO), then red again when dipped into ethanol, with a pungent smell (acetaldehyde). Copper is the catalyst.
铜丝加热时先被氧化：2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO（铜丝变黑）。黑色的 CuO: Heated copper is first oxidised: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO (the wire turns black). The black CuO then reacts with ethanol.
CuO 中的氧夺取乙醇羟基上的 H 和与羟基相连碳上的 H。: The oxygen of CuO takes the H from ethanol's hydroxyl and the H on the carbon bearing the hydroxyl.
C–O 变成 C=O，生成乙醛；氧与两个氢结合成水，CuO 被还原为红色的 Cu: C–O becomes C=O, giving acetaldehyde; the oxygen joins the two hydrogens as water, and CuO is reduced to red Cu.
生成的气体能使溴水、酸性高锰酸钾溶液褪色。温度需迅速升到 170 ℃，140 ℃: The gas decolourises bromine water and acidified potassium permanganate. The temperature must rise quickly to 170 ℃; at 140 ℃ the main product is diethyl ether.
与羟基相连的碳叫 α 碳，相邻的碳叫 β 碳。: The carbon bearing the hydroxyl is the α carbon; its neighbour is the β carbon.
C–OH 键和 β 碳上的 C–H 键同时减弱，β-H 与 –OH 结合。: The C–OH bond and a C–H bond on the β carbon weaken together, and β-H joins the –OH.
相邻两个碳上脱去一个小分子（水），形成碳碳双键——这就是消去反应。: A small molecule (water) is removed from two neighbouring carbons, forming a C=C double bond. This is an elimination reaction.
生成无色油状的溴苯（因溶有溴而呈褐色），导管口出现白雾（HBr 遇水蒸气）。苯不: Colourless oily bromobenzene forms (brown from dissolved bromine), and white fumes appear at the tube outlet (HBr meeting water vapour). Benzene does not decolourise bromine water.
苯环上的六个 π 电子形成稳定的大 π 键，Br₂ 本身不足以进攻。: The six π electrons of benzene form a stable delocalised system that Br₂ alone cannot attack.
FeBr₃ 接受 Br₂ 的一个溴，使另一个溴带正电，成为很强的亲电试剂。: FeBr₃ accepts one bromine of Br₂, leaving the other positively charged and a strong electrophile.
生成 FeBr₄⁻ 和 Br⁺；苯环的 π 电子进攻 Br⁺。: FeBr₄⁻ and Br⁺ form; the π electrons of the ring attack Br⁺.
溴连到苯环上，该碳变成 sp³ 杂化，苯环暂时失去芳香性并带正电。: Bromine bonds to the ring; that carbon becomes sp³ and the ring temporarily loses its aromaticity and carries a positive charge.
C–H 键的电子回到环上，苯环恢复稳定的大 π 键；H⁺ 与 FeBr₄⁻ 生成: The C–H electrons return to the ring, restoring the stable aromatic system; H⁺ and FeBr₄⁻ give HBr, regenerating FeBr₃.
淡蓝色火焰，放出大量热；罩在火焰上方的干冷烧杯内壁出现水珠，倒入澄清石灰水变浑浊: A pale blue flame releases a lot of heat; droplets form inside a dry, cold beaker held over the flame, and limewater poured in turns cloudy.
1 个 CH₄ 分子和 2 个 O₂ 分子。: One CH₄ molecule and two O₂ molecules.
4 个 C–H 键和 2 个 O=O 键全部断开，需要吸收能量（≈ 2 648: Breaking all 4 C–H bonds and 2 O=O bonds absorbs energy (≈ 2 648 kJ/mol).
原子重新组合：形成 2 个 C=O 键和 4 个 O–H 键，放出的能量（≈ 3: The atoms recombine into 2 C=O bonds and 4 O–H bonds, releasing more energy (≈ 3 538 kJ/mol) than was absorbed, so combustion is exothermic.
安静燃烧，发出苍白色火焰，瓶口出现白雾（HCl 遇水蒸气形成盐酸小液滴）。: It burns quietly with a pale flame, and white mist appears at the mouth of the bottle (HCl forming droplets of hydrochloric acid with water vapour).
H–H 键能 436 kJ/mol，Cl–Cl 键能 243 kJ/mol。: Bond energies: H–H 436 kJ/mol, Cl–Cl 243 kJ/mol.
断开 1 mol H–H 和 1 mol Cl–Cl，共吸收 436 + 243: Breaking 1 mol H–H and 1 mol Cl–Cl absorbs 436 + 243 = 679 kJ.
形成 2 mol H–Cl（键能 431 kJ/mol），放出 862 kJ。净: Forming 2 mol H–Cl (bond energy 431 kJ/mol) releases 862 kJ. Net heat released: 862 − 679 = 183 kJ.
剧烈反应，火星四射，放出大量热，生成的铁呈熔融状态落入沙中。可用于焊接钢轨。: A violent reaction throws sparks and releases great heat; the iron produced falls molten into the sand. It is used to weld rails.
左边是铝原子，右边是氧化铁中的 Fe³⁺ 和 O²⁻。铝比铁活泼。: Aluminium atoms on the left; Fe³⁺ and O²⁻ of iron oxide on the right. Aluminium is more reactive than iron.
每个 Al 失去 3 个电子变成 Al³⁺，每个 Fe³⁺ 得到 3 个电子变成: Each Al loses 3 electrons to become Al³⁺; each Fe³⁺ gains 3 electrons to become Fe. Aluminium is the reducing agent and iron oxide the oxidising agent.
O²⁻ 转而与 Al³⁺ 结合成 Al₂O₃，单质铁被置换出来。反应放出的热足以: O²⁻ combines with Al³⁺ instead, forming Al₂O₃ and releasing elemental iron. The heat is enough to melt the iron (about 2 500 ℃).

<p>把电子出现概率为 90% 的区域圈起来，得到的曲面就是常说的<b>原子轨道:
Draw a surface around the region where the electron is found 90% of the time, and you get what we call the shape of an atomic orbital.

s orbitals are spheres; p orbitals are dumbbells, one along each of x, y and z; most d orbitals are four-leaf clovers, five in all.

Warm and cool colours show the positive and negative phase of the wavefunction ψ, not charge. Phase decides whether atoms can bond. Each glowing shell is a surface of equal probability; the deeper inside, the higher the probability density.
<p>径向分布函数 <b>P(r) = r²R²</b> 表示电子出现在半径 r:
The radial distribution function P(r) = r²R² gives the probability of finding the electron in a thin spherical shell at radius r.

The 1s peak lies exactly at r = a₀ (the Bohr radius). Between the peaks of 2s and 3s are spheres where the probability is zero, called radial nodes; there are n − l − 1 of them.

In the slice, dark rings are radial nodes and dark straight lines are angular nodes.

<p><b>核膜</b>是双层膜，把核内物质与细胞质分开。外膜与内质网相连，表面:
The nuclear envelope is a double membrane that separates the nuclear contents from the cytoplasm. Its outer membrane is continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum and is also studded with ribosomes.

Nuclear pores span both membranes of the envelope, allowing frequent exchange of materials and information between nucleus and cytoplasm: mRNA leaves the nucleus here, and proteins that assemble ribosomes enter here. Nuclear pores are selective; DNA cannot pass through.

The nucleolus is involved in synthesizing a type of RNA (rRNA) and in forming ribosomes.

Chromatin consists mainly of DNA and protein and carries the genetic information. Chromatin and chromosomes are the same material in two different states at different stages of the cell cycle.
有氧呼吸的主要场所，细胞的“动力车间”: Main site of aerobic respiration, the "powerhouse of the cell"
<p>线粒体有内、外两层膜。<b>内膜</b>向内折叠形成<b>嵴</b>，大大:
A mitochondrion has two membranes, inner and outer. The inner membrane folds inward to form cristae, greatly increasing its surface area; the enzymes for the third stage of aerobic respiration are located on the inner membrane.

The matrix contains the enzymes for the second stage of aerobic respiration, along with a small amount of DNA and ribosomes, so it can make some of its own proteins.

About 95% of the energy a cell needs comes from mitochondria. Metabolically active cells (such as cardiac muscle cells) contain especially many mitochondria.

Chloroplasts are flattened ellipsoids or spheres enclosed by a double membrane.

Inside are many grana; each granum is a stack of disc-shaped thylakoids, and grana are connected by lamellae. The pigments that absorb light and the enzymes of the light reactions are all on the thylakoid membranes, which greatly increases the light-harvesting area.

The stroma contains the enzymes of the dark reactions (Calvin cycle), as well as a small amount of DNA and ribosomes. Products of photosynthesis can be stored temporarily as starch grains.
蛋白质合成和加工的场所: Site of protein synthesis and processing
<p>内质网是由膜围成的管状、泡状或扁平囊状结构连接形成的网状结构，内腔彼此相通:
The endoplasmic reticulum is a network of membrane-bounded tubules, vesicles and flattened sacs whose internal spaces (lumen) are all connected. It is the pathway for synthesizing, processing and transporting proteins and other macromolecules.

The membrane of the rough endoplasmic reticulum is studded with many ribosomes. Secretory proteins made on these ribosomes enter the ER lumen, where they are folded, glycosylated and otherwise initially processed.

Inward, the ER membrane is continuous with the outer nuclear membrane; outward, it can connect with the plasma membrane.
<p>光面内质网的膜上没有核糖体，多呈分支的小管状。</p><p>它是合成脂质（:
The membrane of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum has no ribosomes and is mostly made of branching tubules.

It is the site of lipid synthesis (e.g. phospholipids and steroid hormones). In liver cells it helps detoxify drugs and poisons; in muscle cells (as the sarcoplasmic reticulum) it stores calcium ions.
对蛋白质进行加工、分类和包装的“车间”及“发送站”: The "factory" and "shipping center" that processes, sorts and packages proteins
<p>高尔基体由一摞弯曲的扁平囊（潴泡）和周围的囊泡组成，有明确的方向：<b>顺:
The Golgi apparatus is a stack of curved, flattened sacs (cisternae) surrounded by vesicles, with a clear polarity: the cis face faces the ER and receives incoming vesicles; the trans face faces the plasma membrane, sorts and packages products, and buds off new vesicles.

Proteins from the ER are further modified here and then sent to the plasma membrane, to lysosomes, or secreted out of the cell.

In plant cells, the Golgi apparatus is also involved in cell wall formation.
<p>溶酶体内含多种<b>水解酶</b>，能分解衰老、损伤的细胞器，吞噬并杀死侵:
Lysosomes contain many hydrolytic enzymes that break down aged or damaged organelles and engulf and kill viruses or bacteria that invade the cell.

Proton pumps in the lysosomal membrane pump H⁺ into the lumen, keeping it acidic (pH≈5), where the hydrolytic enzymes work best; even if a few enzymes leak into the neutral cytosol, they are largely inactive.
分解过氧化氢与脂肪酸（大学拓展）: Breaks down hydrogen peroxide and fatty acids (beyond the syllabus)
<p>过氧化物酶体是单层膜的小泡，内含过氧化氢酶等多种氧化酶，常见尿酸氧化酶形成:
A peroxisome is a small vesicle bounded by a single membrane, containing catalase and various other oxidases; it often has a crystalline core of urate oxidase.

It breaks down toxic H₂O₂ into water and oxygen and takes part in fatty acid oxidation.
调节细胞内的环境，使植物细胞保持坚挺: Regulates the cell's internal environment and keeps plant cells firm
<p>液泡由单层的<b>液泡膜</b>围成，内有<b>细胞液</b>，含糖类、无:
The vacuole is bounded by a single membrane, the tonoplast, and filled with cell sap containing sugars, inorganic salts, pigments and proteins. The colors of petals and fruits mostly come from anthocyanins in the vacuole.

In a mature plant cell, the large central vacuole can occupy 90% of the cell volume, pushing the cytoplasm and nucleus into a thin layer against the cell wall. The turgor pressure created when the vacuole takes up water keeps plant cells firm.
<p>核糖体没有膜结构，由 rRNA 和蛋白质构成，分为<b>大亚基</b>和<:
Ribosomes have no membrane; they are made of rRNA and protein and consist of a large subunit and a small subunit, with mRNA threading between them.

Some ribosomes are bound to the ER (making secretory and membrane proteins), while others are free in the cytosol (making intracellular proteins). Prokaryotic cells also have ribosomes, the only organelle prokaryotes possess.
<p>中心体见于动物和某些低等植物细胞，由两个<b>互相垂直</b>排列的中心粒:
The centrosome is found in animal cells and some lower plant cells. It consists of two centrioles arranged at right angles to each other plus surrounding material, and has no membrane.

Each centriole is a cylinder of 9 triplets of microtubules (the "9×3" arrangement). The centrosome is the microtubule-organizing center: in interphase it sends out radiating microtubules, and during division it sends out astral rays that form the spindle.
<p>细胞膜主要由<b>脂质</b>（磷脂最丰富）和<b>蛋白质</b>组成，还:
The plasma membrane consists mainly of lipids (phospholipids are most abundant) and proteins, with a small amount of carbohydrate.

It has three functions: separating the cell from its environment, controlling what enters and leaves the cell, and enabling communication between cells.

Its structural feature is a degree of fluidity; its functional feature is selective permeability. Chapters 5 and 6 zoom in to the molecular scale for a closer look.
<p>植物细胞壁的主要成分是<b>纤维素和果胶</b>，具有<b>全透性</b>:
The plant cell wall is made mainly of cellulose and pectin. It is fully permeable and supports and protects the cell.

Neighboring cells are connected through plasmodesmata, one way plant cells communicate with each other.
维持细胞形态，锚定并支撑细胞器: Maintains cell shape; anchors and supports organelles
<p>细胞骨架是由<b>蛋白质纤维</b>组成的网架结构，包括微管、微丝和中间纤:
The cytoskeleton is a network of protein fibers, including microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments.

It maintains cell shape, anchors and supports many organelles, and is closely involved in cell movement, division and differentiation, as well as material transport, energy conversion and information transfer.
<p>囊泡是由单层膜包裹的小泡，从内质网、高尔基体或细胞膜上“出芽”形成，再与目:
Vesicles are small sacs enclosed by a single membrane. They "bud" from the ER, the Golgi apparatus or the plasma membrane, then fuse with a target membrane to deliver their contents.

Vesicle transport links the various biological membranes closely in structure and function, forming the biomembrane system (endomembrane system).
原核细胞 DNA 集中的区域: Region where prokaryotic DNA is concentrated
<p>原核细胞没有以核膜为界限的细胞核。它的 DNA 是一个<b>大型环状</b:
Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus bounded by a nuclear envelope. Their DNA is a single large circular molecule, coiled and folded in a central region of the cell called the nucleoid.

Prokaryotic DNA does not combine with proteins to form chromosomes.
拟核之外的小型环状 DNA: Small circular DNA outside the nucleoid
<p>质粒是存在于拟核之外的小型环状 DNA 分子，能自主复制，常携带抗药性等基:
Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules outside the nucleoid. They replicate independently and often carry genes such as antibiotic resistance.

In genetic engineering, plasmids are commonly used as vectors to carry target genes.
<p>某些细菌在细胞壁外有一层黏液状的荚膜，主要由多糖构成，能保护细菌、帮助其黏: Some bacteria have a slimy capsule outside the cell wall, made mainly of polysaccharides. It protects the bacterium, helps it stick to surfaces, and resists phagocytosis by the host.
<p>细菌鞭毛是由鞭毛蛋白组成的螺旋状细丝，基部的“分子马达”嵌在细胞膜中，借助:
A bacterial flagellum is a helical filament made of flagellin. A "molecular motor" at its base, embedded in the plasma membrane, uses the H⁺ gradient across the membrane to spin the flagellum like a propeller, at up to several hundred revolutions per second.

Its structure is completely different from that of eukaryotic flagella (9+2 microtubule arrangement).
黏附与遗传物质的传递: Attachment and transfer of genetic material
<p>菌毛比鞭毛短而直、数量多，帮助细菌黏附在宿主细胞表面；性菌毛还能在细菌之间: Pili are shorter, straighter and more numerous than flagella and help bacteria attach to host cell surfaces; sex pili can also transfer plasmids between bacteria.
<p>细菌细胞壁的主要成分是<b>肽聚糖</b>，与植物细胞壁（纤维素和果胶）不: The bacterial cell wall is made mainly of peptidoglycan, unlike the plant cell wall (cellulose and pectin). Penicillin inhibits peptidoglycan synthesis, so it can kill bacteria without harming human cells.

<p>动物细胞与植物细胞都有细胞膜、细胞质和细胞核，也都有线粒体、内质网、高尔基:
Both animal and plant cells have a plasma membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus, as well as organelles such as mitochondria, ER, Golgi apparatus and ribosomes.

Unique to plant cells: cell wall, chloroplasts (in green tissues), large central vacuole.

Unique to animal cells: centrosome (also in lower plant cells); lysosomes are found mainly in animal cells.

<p>根据有无<b>以核膜为界限的细胞核</b>，细胞分为原核细胞和真核细胞。细:
Cells are classified as prokaryotic or eukaryotic by whether they have a nucleus bounded by a nuclear envelope. Bacteria and cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are prokaryotes; animals, plants and fungi are eukaryotes.

Prokaryotic DNA is concentrated in the nucleoid, with no nuclear envelope or nucleolus; the only organelle is the ribosome.

<p>放大到分子尺度（约 1 亿倍），细胞膜的基本支架是<b>磷脂双分子层</b:
Zoomed to the molecular scale (about 100 million times), the basic framework of the plasma membrane is the phospholipid bilayer: the hydrophilic heads of phospholipids face the watery environment on both sides, and the hydrophobic tails point inward toward each other.

Proteins may sit on the surface, be partly or fully embedded, or span the entire bilayer.

On the outer surface, carbohydrates bind to proteins to form glycoproteins and to lipids to form glycolipids, together called the glycocalyx, which is closely involved in cell recognition and signaling.

Watch closely: phospholipids keep moving sideways and most proteins can move too, so the membrane is fluid.
<p><b>被动运输</b>：顺浓度梯度，不消耗能量。<br>· <b>自由扩散:
Passive transport: down the concentration gradient, no energy used.
· Simple diffusion: O₂, CO₂, glycerol, ethanol, etc. pass directly through the phospholipid bilayer.
· Facilitated diffusion: via channel proteins (water, K⁺) or carrier proteins (glucose entering red blood cells).

Active transport: against the concentration gradient, requires carrier proteins and uses ATP, e.g. the sodium–potassium pump.

Endocytosis and exocytosis: macromolecules and particles enter and leave the cell through membrane fluidity, using energy.

Scientists injected ³H-labeled leucine into guinea pig pancreatic acinar cells and tracked where the radioactivity appeared in sequence (isotope labeling, pulse–chase).

Polypeptide made on ribosomes → enters the rough endoplasmic reticulum for processing and folding → ER buds off vesicles → vesicles fuse with the Golgi apparatus for further modification → Golgi buds off vesicles → vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane and the protein is secreted by exocytosis.

Energy for the whole process comes mainly from mitochondria.

The cytoskeleton is made of three kinds of protein fibers: microtubules (thickest, about 25 nm, radiating from the centrosome), microfilaments (thinnest, about 7 nm, i.e. actin filaments, forming a dense mesh beneath the plasma membrane) and intermediate filaments (about 10 nm, adding strength like ropes).

Motor proteins "walk" along the cytoskeleton carrying cargo: kinesin moves toward the plus end (cell periphery), dynein toward the minus end (centrosome). Each step hydrolyzes one ATP.

In plant cells, myosin drags the cytoplasm along microfilaments, and chloroplasts are carried around the central vacuole; this is the cytoplasmic streaming (cyclosis) seen in the lab.
O₂、CO₂ 等小分子直接穿过磷脂双分子层，从高浓度一侧扩散到低浓度一侧。不需要: Small molecules such as O₂ and CO₂ pass directly through the phospholipid bilayer from the high-concentration side to the low-concentration side. No transport protein or energy is needed; the rate is proportional to the concentration difference.
水分子经<b>水通道蛋白</b>单行通过，K⁺ 经离子通道顺浓度梯度流出。通道蛋: Water molecules pass single file through aquaporins, and K⁺ flows out through ion channels down its concentration gradient. Channel proteins only let through molecules of suitable size and charge, and the molecules do not bind to the channel protein.
葡萄糖进入红细胞时，先与<b>载体蛋白</b>结合，载体蛋白构象改变，把它转到膜: When glucose enters a red blood cell, it first binds to a carrier protein, which changes shape and releases it on the other side of the membrane. Carriers are limited in number, so the transport rate saturates at large concentration differences.
钠钾泵每水解 1 个 ATP，就把 <b>3 个 Na⁺ 泵出</b>、<b>2: For each ATP hydrolyzed, the sodium–potassium pump moves 3 Na⁺ out of and 2 K⁺ into the cell, both against their concentration gradients. Active transport requires carrier proteins and energy supplied by cellular respiration.

<p>激光沿量角盘射向平面镜的中心 O。过入射点作垂直于镜面的<b>法线</b>:

The angle between the incident ray and the normal is the angle of incidence i; the angle between the reflected ray and the normal is the angle of reflection r.

r = i

The reflected ray, the incident ray and the normal lie in the same plane, and the reflected and incident rays are on opposite sides of the normal.

Drag the laser pointer around the disk, or use the slider to change the angle of incidence, and press Record to save each pair of i and r. If light is sent back along the reflected ray, it leaves along the original incident ray: light paths are reversible.

A plane mirror forms an upright, same-size virtual image, symmetric to the object about the mirror. <p>激光从空气斜射入<b>半圆形玻璃砖</b>的平面中心。光进入玻璃后偏向法线:
A laser travels obliquely from air into the center of the flat face of a semicircular glass block. Inside the glass the light bends toward the normal, so the angle of refraction r is smaller than the angle of incidence i. It leaves through the curved face along a radius without bending again, which makes reading easy.

Measure several pairs of i and r: i and r are not proportional, but their sines are. This is the law of refraction:

n is the refractive index of the medium. Plot sin i against sin r in the data dock; the slope is n. Switch to water (1.33) or diamond (2.42) to compare.

<p>一束白光穿过三棱镜后，在光屏上展开成<b>红、橙、黄、绿、蓝、靛、紫</b:
A beam of white light passing through a triangular prism spreads out on the screen into a band of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. This is dispersion. Newton used this experiment to show that white light is a mixture of many colors.

The same glass has a different refractive index for each color: violet has the largest index and bends the most; red has the smallest and bends the least.

Switch to a single-color red laser: after the prism it only bends and no longer splits. Add an inverted prism behind it, and the colors recombine into white light.

<p>眼睛像一架照相机：<b>晶状体</b>相当于凸透镜，<b>视网膜</b>相:
The eye works like a camera: the crystalline lens acts as a convex lens and the retina acts as the screen. The ciliary muscles change the thickness (focal length) of the lens so that objects near and far all form sharp images on the retina.

Nearsighted (myopic) eye: the eyeball is too long (or the lens too thick), so images of distant objects fall in front of the retina and distant things look blurry. It is corrected with a concave lens, which spreads the light out a little.

Farsighted (hyperopic) eye: images fall behind the retina and near things look blurry. It is corrected with a convex lens.

prescription (×100) = optical power × 100 = 100 / f (f in m)

<p>激光照到相距很近的两条狭缝上，两缝相当于两个<b>相干光源</b>。两列光:
A laser falls on two very close slits, which act as two coherent sources. The two light waves superpose on the screen: where the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths they reinforce, giving bright fringes; where it is an odd number of half wavelengths they cancel, giving dark fringes.

Δx = L λ / d

The spacing Δx between adjacent bright fringes is proportional to the screen distance L and the wavelength λ, and inversely proportional to the slit separation d. The colored ripples on the bench illustrate the superposition of the two waves (wavelength exaggerated).

After light passes through a very narrow single slit, the screen shows a wide, bright central fringe with narrower, dimmer fringes on each side. This is diffraction. The narrower the slit, the wider the central fringe and the more obvious the diffraction.

central fringe half-width x₁ = L λ / a

Unlike double-slit fringes (equally spaced), in single-slit diffraction the central bright fringe is twice as wide as the others.

A diffraction grating has a large number of equally spaced slits, giving very sharp, bright principal maxima: d sinθ = kλ. With white light each order becomes a colored spectrum, with violet deviated least and red most: exactly the opposite of a prism.

<p>一排质点由弹性力相互连接。最左边的质点在外力作用下振动，带动相邻质点依次振:
A row of particles is linked by elastic forces. The leftmost particle oscillates under an external force and sets its neighbors oscillating one after another. In this way the form of the vibration and its energy propagate outward, forming a mechanical wave.

Note that the particles themselves do not travel with the wave; each only oscillates about its own equilibrium position (watch the red particle). If the particles oscillate perpendicular to the direction of propagation, it is a transverse wave; if along the same line, it is a longitudinal wave, with rarefactions and compressions.

v = λ f = λ / T

<p>在绳的一端甩出一个脉冲，脉冲传到另一端后被<b>反射</b>回来。</p>:
Flick a pulse from one end of the rope. When the pulse reaches the other end, it is reflected back.

· Fixed end: the end of the rope is clamped and cannot move. The reflected wave is inverted relative to the incident wave (a crest becomes a trough), as if half a wavelength were lost. This is the half-wave loss (phase reversal).
· Free end: the end of the rope is looped around a smooth vertical rod and can slide freely. The reflected wave is in phase with the incident wave.

The wave speed is the same before and after reflection.

<p>几列波相遇时，每个质点的位移等于各列波单独引起的位移之和——<b>波的叠加:
When several waves meet, the displacement of each particle equals the sum of the displacements each wave would cause on its own. This is the principle of superposition. After meeting, each wave keeps its original shape and travels on.

The source at the left end oscillates continuously; the wave reflects at the fixed right end, and the incident and reflected waves superpose. When the rope length is exactly an integer multiple of half a wavelength, a stable standing wave forms: some points never move (nodes) and some have the largest amplitude (antinodes).

fₙ = n v / 2L (n = 1, 2, 3 …)

This is how the strings of a guitar or violin make sound.

Two sources that vibrate in exactly the same way (coherent sources) set up water waves. Where the path difference from a point to the two sources is an integer multiple of the wavelength, the vibration is reinforced; where it is an odd multiple of half a wavelength, the vibration is weakened. Stable regions of reinforcement and cancellation alternate across the surface. This is wave interference.

Δr = kλ constructive Δr = (2k+1)λ/2 destructive

Switch to single slit: a plane wave passing through a slit in a barrier spreads out in all directions. This is diffraction. Diffraction is most noticeable when the slit is narrower than, or about the same as, the wavelength.

When a sound source approaches an observer, the wavefronts ahead of it are "squeezed" together and the wavelength gets shorter, so the observer hears a higher frequency. When the source moves away, the wavelength gets longer and the frequency drops. This is the Doppler effect:

f′ = f · v / (v ∓ vₛ)

Turn on the sound and switch the "Listener position" to hear the pitch change. When the source moves faster than sound, the wavefronts pile up into a cone, the Mach cone, producing a sonic boom.

<p>声音由物体振动产生，以声波的形式传播。示波器显示麦克风接收到的波形：</p:
Sound is produced by vibrating objects and travels as sound waves. The oscilloscope shows the waveform picked up by the microphone:

· Loudness is set by the amplitude
· Pitch is set by the frequency
· Timbre is set by the waveform (its mix of harmonics). A tuning fork gives an almost pure sine wave; a piano or violin is rich in harmonics.

Strike a tuning fork and hold it over the mouth of the resonance tube. Adjust the water level to change the length L of the air column. When

L = (2n − 1) λ / 4

the air column resonates and the sound becomes clearly louder. The difference λ/2 between two resonance lengths lets you measure the speed of sound.

<p>点电荷周围的电场 E = kQ/r²，多个电荷的电场按矢量<b>叠加</b:
The field of a point charge is E = kQ/r²; the fields of several charges superpose as vectors. Electric field lines picture the field: the tangent at each point gives the field direction, and the line density shows the field strength. Field lines start on positive charges (or at infinity) and end on negative charges (or at infinity); they never cross and never close on themselves.

The electric potential φ = kQ/r is a scalar and simply adds up. Points of equal potential form equipotential lines:

Equipotentials are everywhere perpendicular to field lines; potential decreases along a field line

When a test charge q moves from A to B, the work done by the electric field is

WAB = q (φA − φB) = q UAB

It depends only on the start and end points, not on the path — just like the work done by gravity. So we can define the electric potential energy Ep = qφ: when the field does positive work, the potential energy decreases; when it does negative work, the potential energy increases.

Two parallel metal plates, close together and insulated from each other, form a parallel-plate capacitor. Its capacitance is

C = εr S / (4πkd) = εrε0 S / d

After charging, disconnect the source: the charge Q on the plates stays constant, and from U = Q/C, increasing d, reducing the overlapping area S, or removing the dielectric makes C smaller and the deflection of the electrometer needle (U) larger. The field between the plates, E = U/d = Q/(εrε0S), does not depend on d.

If the capacitor stays connected to the source, U is constant, and Q and E change as d changes. Record several data sets: the C - 1/d graph is a straight line through the origin.

Mass spectrometer: ions accelerated through voltage U enter a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly through slit S, travel half a circle and strike the photographic plate:

qU = ½mv² r = mv/(qB) = √(2mU/q) / B

For isotopes with the same charge, the heavier the ion, the larger the radius, so they form separate spectral lines on the plate, with r₁ : r₂ = √m₁ : √m₂. This is how Aston discovered the isotopes of neon.

Cyclotron: two D-shaped electrodes (dees) sit in a uniform magnetic field with an alternating voltage across the gap. The particle is accelerated each time it crosses the gap and its radius keeps growing, but the period T = 2πm/(qB) is independent of speed, so the frequency of the alternating voltage can stay fixed. The final kinetic energy

Ek = q²B²R² / (2m)

depends only on B and the dee radius R, not on the accelerating voltage.

A rectangular coil rotates at constant speed in a uniform field about an axis perpendicular to the field. Sides ab and cd cut the field lines, producing an alternating current whose magnitude and direction vary periodically. Timing from the neutral plane:

e = Em sin ωt Em = NBSω

The neutral plane is where the coil plane is perpendicular to the field: here the flux is at its maximum, but no side cuts the field lines, so the emf is zero. After 90° the flux is zero and the emf is maximum. Each time the coil passes the neutral plane, the current reverses direction.

Use the microscope following the textbook steps. The checklist below ticks off each step, and any mistakes are logged in the data dock.

1. Carrying and placing: grip the arm with your right hand and support the base with your left; set it on the bench slightly to the left.

2. Adjusting the light: turn the nosepiece so the low-power objective is over the stage aperture; line up a large opening of the diaphragm with the aperture; looking into the eyepiece with your left eye, turn the mirror until you see a bright, round field.

3. Observing: put the slide on the stage with the specimen centred over the aperture and hold it with the stage clips. Turn the coarse focus knob to lower the tube slowly, watching the objective from the side, until it is close to the slide; then look into the eyepiece and turn the coarse knob the other way to raise the tube slowly until the image appears, and finally turn the fine focus knob slightly to sharpen it.

In this lesson, dragging in the field is set to “push the slide”: whichever way your hand pushes the slide, the image moves the opposite way.

Image is off to the upper left → move the slide toward the upper left and the image returns to the centre

<p>高倍镜下视野范围小，所以必须<b>先在低倍镜下找到目标</b>，把它移到视:
The field of view is small under high power, so you must first find the target under low power, move it to the center of the field, and then turn the revolving nosepiece to the high-power objective.

After switching to high power:

· The field becomes smaller and darker: open the diaphragm or switch to the concave mirror;
· Depth of field becomes shallower: use only the fine focus knob — a single click of the coarse focus knob may crush the slide;
· You see fewer cells, and each cell looks larger.

Field diameter = field number ÷ objective magnification　Brightness ∝ (NA ÷ objective magnification)²

The target cell is circled with a dashed line. The "Imaging parameters" table in the data dock compares the four objectives.

There is a speck in the field of view. It may be on the eyepiece, the objective or the slide.

· Rotate the eyepiece: the speck turns with it → on the eyepiece;
· Move the slide: the speck moves with it → on the slide;
· Neither moves it, and it disappears when you change objectives → on the objective.

<p>撕下洋葱鳞片叶<b>内表皮</b>，展平在清水中，盖上盖玻片。未染色时细胞:
Peel off the inner epidermis of an onion bulb scale, spread it flat in a drop of water and add a coverslip. Unstained cells are almost transparent and only the cell walls are clear — try closing the diaphragm: transparent structures will show their outlines.

Click the iodine solution on the bench and add it at one edge of the coverslip, then click the filter paper to draw it from the other edge (wicking). The iodine gradually flows across the specimen: nuclei stain dark brown and nucleoli become clearly visible.

Basic structures of a plant cell: cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, vacuole. Onion epidermal cells have one large central vacuole, which often pushes the nucleus to the edge of the cell.

Turn the fine focus knob at 40×: cells are about 25 µm thick, and you see different structures when the focal plane is at the top surface, the middle or the bottom surface.

打开结构标注，悬停识别各结构: Turn on structure labels and hover to identify each structure
<p>用消毒牙签在口腔内侧壁轻刮，涂在滴有<b>生理盐水</b>的载玻片上（用清:
Gently scrape the inside of the cheek with a sterile toothpick and smear it on a slide with a drop of physiological saline (in plain water the cells absorb water and burst), then add a coverslip.

Cheek epithelial cells are flat and irregular in shape, often clumped and overlapping, with folded edges; the nucleus is small and central. They are so thin they are almost invisible unstained; after staining with methylene blue the nuclei turn dark blue. Oral bacteria are often attached to the cell surface.

Compared with onion epidermal cells: animal cells have no cell wall and no large vacuole, and their shape is not fixed.
在 10× 下找到细胞团，缩小光圈: Find a cluster of cells at 10× and close down the diaphragm
滴加亚甲蓝并引流: Add methylene blue and wick it through
换 40× 观察细胞核与细菌: Switch to 40× to observe nuclei and bacteria
在数据坞对比动植物细胞: Compare plant and animal cells in the data dock
<p>从草履虫培养液的<b>表层</b>吸一滴（表层氧气多，草履虫多），放几丝<:
Take a drop from the surface layer of a Paramecium culture (more oxygen there, so more paramecia), add a few cotton fibers to slow them down, and add a coverslip.

Paramecium is a single-celled organism shaped like an upside-down slipper, about 200 µm long. Its surface is covered with cilia, whose beating makes it spin forward; when it hits an obstacle it backs up, turns and moves forward again.

At 10× you can see: the oral groove, food vacuoles (carried by the flowing cytoplasm), two contractile vacuoles (with radiating collecting canals, contracting regularly to expel excess water), and the macronucleus and micronucleus.

They swim fast — add cotton fibers and track them under low power.
打开或关闭棉花纤维，比较运动: Add or remove cotton fibers and compare the movement
换 10×，跟踪一只草履虫: Switch to 10× and track one paramecium
数一数伸缩泡收缩的频率: Count how often the contractile vacuoles contract
<p><b>黑藻</b>的小叶只有一两层细胞，可以直接制片观察。细胞里的<b>叶:
The small leaves of Hydrilla are only one or two cell layers thick and can be mounted directly. The chloroplasts in the cells are flattened ellipsoids that flow along the cell edge around the central vacuole — this is cytoplasmic streaming. Using the chloroplasts as markers, you can tell the direction of flow.

Switch to the broad bean leaf lower epidermis slide: the epidermal cells interlock like jigsaw pieces; pairs of crescent-shaped guard cells surround each stoma. Guard cells contain chloroplasts; ordinary epidermal cells do not.

In the leaf cross-section slide you can see the upper and lower epidermis, palisade tissue, spongy tissue and veins.
在 40× 下观察黑藻叶绿体的流动方向: Observe the direction of chloroplast flow in Hydrilla at 40×
换蚕豆叶下表皮，找到气孔和保卫细胞: Switch to broad bean lower epidermis; find stomata and guard cells
换叶片横切，辨认各层组织: Switch to the leaf cross-section and identify each tissue layer
<p>紫色洋葱鳞片叶<b>外表皮</b>细胞的液泡含花青素，便于观察原生质层的位:
The vacuoles of purple onion bulb scale outer epidermis cells contain anthocyanin, which makes the position of the protoplast layer easy to see.

Add 0.3 g/mL sucrose solution at one edge of the coverslip and draw it through with filter paper from the other edge. The outside solution is more concentrated than the cell sap, so the cells lose water and the protoplast layer (cell membrane, tonoplast and the cytoplasm between them) gradually separates from the cell wall — starting at the corners; the vacuole shrinks and the purple deepens.

Then add water in the same way: the cells take up water and deplasmolysis occurs.

Elasticity of the protoplast layer > elasticity of the cell wall

The data dock records how the average protoplast area of cells in the field changes over time.
滴加蔗糖溶液并引流: Add sucrose solution and wick it through
观察原生质层与细胞壁分离: Observe the protoplast layer separating from the cell wall
滴加清水并引流，观察复原: Add water, wick it through and observe recovery
<p>洋葱根尖经过<b>解离</b>（盐酸 + 酒精，使细胞分离）→ <b>漂洗:
Onion root tips go through dissociation (hydrochloric acid + alcohol, to separate the cells) → rinsing → staining (crystal violet solution, to color the chromosomes) → mounting (squashing to spread the cells).

First find the meristematic zone under low power: the cells are square, tightly packed, and many are dividing; cells of the root cap and elongation zone look different.

After switching to high power, click a cell and decide which stage it is in: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase or telophase. The data dock counts cells in each stage and calculates the mitotic index.

Ratio of cell numbers in each stage ≈ ratio of time spent in each stage

Note: the cells are dead after dissociation, so you see static cells — you cannot watch one cell divide continuously.
在 4× 下找到根尖分生区: Find the meristematic zone of the root tip at 4×
换 40×，观察各时期细胞: Switch to 40× and observe cells in each stage
点击细胞判断时期，累计 30 个以上: Click cells to classify their stage — at least 30 in total
<p>人血涂片（瑞氏染色）中最多的是<b>红细胞</b>：两面凹的圆盘，中央较薄:
The most numerous cells in a human blood smear (Wright stain) are red blood cells: biconcave discs, thinner and paler in the center, with no nucleus. White blood cells are few and have nuclei: neutrophils have nuclei with 2~5 lobes, lymphocytes have large round nuclei, monocytes are the largest with kidney-shaped nuclei, and eosinophils contain orange-red granules. Platelets are tiny and have no nucleus.

The 100× objective is an oil immersion lens: its numerical aperture is 1.25, and you must put a drop of cedarwood oil on the coverslip, otherwise light is refracted and totally reflected at the glass–air interface and the image is blurry. Its working distance is only 0.15 mm.

Compare with a frog blood smear: frog red blood cells are oval and have nuclei.
在 40× 下找到细胞分布均匀的区域: Find an area with evenly spread cells at 40×
不加油直接换 100×，观察图像: Switch to 100× without oil and observe the image
点香柏油滴在盖玻片上，再观察: Click the cedarwood oil to drop it on the coverslip, then observe again
找出各种白细胞；换蛙血涂片对比: Find each type of white blood cell; compare with a frog blood smear
<p><b>目镜测微尺</b>装在目镜里，刻度随目镜放大，实际代表的长度随物镜倍:
The ocular micrometer sits inside the eyepiece; its scale is magnified with the eyepiece, and the real length each division represents changes with the objective, so it must be calibrated first. The stage micrometer is a slide with a precise scale: 1 mm divided into 100 divisions, 10 µm each.

Rotate the eyepiece so the two scales are parallel, move the stage micrometer so both 0 marks line up, then look to the right for the place where the two scales coincide again:

Length per eyepiece division = stage divisions × 10 µm ÷ eyepiece divisions

Enter the readings in the data dock and calibrate. Then switch to a cell slide (do not change the objective) and drag a line in the field to measure cell length.
转动目镜使两尺平行，对齐 0 刻度: Rotate the eyepiece so the scales are parallel and align the 0 marks
找到重合刻度，填写格数并标定: Find coinciding marks, enter the division counts and calibrate
换洋葱表皮或酵母，测量细胞: Switch to onion epidermis or yeast and measure cells
换物镜后重新标定，比较每格长度: Recalibrate after changing objectives and compare the length per division
<p>血球计数板的计数室是 1 mm × 1 mm 的方格，深 0.1 mm，分:
The counting chamber of the hemocytometer is a 1 mm × 1 mm grid, 0.1 mm deep, divided into 25 medium squares of 16 small squares each.

Put on the coverslip first, then add yeast culture at the edge of the coverslip and let it seep in by itself. Wait a moment for the yeast to settle to the bottom of the chamber before counting.

Count the yeast in the 5 medium squares at the four corners and the center (80 small squares in all). Click a yeast cell to count it. For cells on the grid lines, count the top and left lines, not the bottom and right; a budding yeast counts as two only when the bud is at least half the size of the mother cell.

Yeast per mL = count in 80 small squares ÷ 80 × 400 × 10⁴ × dilution factor
移到第一个中方格，点击计数: Move to the first medium square and click to count
依次数完 5 个中方格: Count all 5 medium squares in turn
计算培养液中的酵母菌密度: Calculate the yeast density of the culture
明场、暗场与相差: Bright field, dark field and phase contrast
<p>活细胞大多是透明的，只改变光的<b>相位</b>，不改变亮度，在明场下很难:
Most living cells are transparent: they only change the phase of light, not its brightness, so they are hard to see in bright field.

· Bright field: closing the aperture diaphragm raises contrast but lowers resolution; slight defocus gives transparent structures bright or dark edges.
· Dark field: blocks direct light and lets only light scattered by the specimen enter the objective — cell outlines and tiny particles glow on a black background.
· Phase contrast: a phase plate converts optical path differences into brightness differences, so transparent cells show clearly, with bright halos at their edges.

Resolution d = λ ÷ (NA objective + NA condenser)

Switch to diatom, Paramecium and other slides and compare the three methods.

换硅藻玻片再比较: Switch to the diatom slide and compare again

<p>硅藻的细胞壁由<b>二氧化硅</b>构成，像带盖的盒子，壳面上有排列整齐的:
The diatom cell wall is made of silica, like a box with a lid, and its valve surface bears regularly arranged striae and pores. Cleaned frustules are almost colorless and transparent, a classic specimen for testing objective resolution.

The striae of Pleurosigma are about 0.55 µm apart: they cannot be resolved with the 40× objective, only with the 100× oil-immersion objective (smaller field, iris diaphragm opened wider). Compare the results in brightfield, darkfield and phase contrast.
换 40× 观察胞质环流: Switch to 40× to observe cytoplasmic streaming
胞质环流：活细胞的细胞质沿着中央大液泡的周围循环流动，叶绿体随之移动，可作为流动: Cytoplasmic streaming: in living cells the cytoplasm circulates around the large central vacuole, carrying the chloroplasts along, which serve as markers of the flow. The microscope gives an inverted image (rotated 180°), which does not change the direction of streaming: clockwise in the field of view is also clockwise in reality. Adjacent cells often stream in opposite directions; streaming speeds up with a moderate rise in temperature and stronger light.

刻度说明：1 mm 分为 100 格: Scale note: 1 mm divided into 100 divisions

细胞壁与原生质层之间的外界溶液: External solution between cell wall and protoplast layer
紫色洋葱鳞片叶外表皮: Purple onion scale leaf outer epidermis
<p>草履虫靠纤毛摆动前进，同时绕身体长轴旋转，所以走的是螺旋形路线。碰到障碍时:
A paramecium swims forward by beating its cilia while rotating around its long axis, so it follows a spiral path. When it hits an obstacle the cilia beat in reverse: it first backs up, then turns at an angle and swims forward again (the avoiding reaction).

The collecting canals around each contractile vacuole gather water and empty it into the vacuole; once swollen, the vacuole suddenly contracts and expels the excess water from the cell. The two contractile vacuoles alternate.
<p>花粉粒的<b>外壁</b>有各种纹饰（刺、网纹）和<b>萌发孔 / 萌发沟:
The exine of pollen grains bears various ornaments (spines, reticulate patterns) and germination pores / furrows; their shape is used to identify plants. Pine pollen has two air sacs, suited to wind pollination; sunflower and hibiscus pollen are spiny, typical of insect pollination.

Pollen grains are fairly thick: turn the fine focus knob to see in turn the surface ornament, the outline in optical section, and the ornament on the far side.
<p><b>洋葱根尖</b>（2n = 16）压片，甲紫染色。分生区细胞呈正方形:
Squash of an onion root tip (2n = 16), stained with crystal violet. Meristematic zone cells are square, tightly packed, with large nuclei; elongation zone cells become longer and no longer divide.

Most cells in the field are in interphase, because interphase takes up the longest part of the cell cycle.
<p>水绵的叶绿体呈带状、螺旋排列。上下调节细准焦螺旋：靠近你的一半螺旋带与远离: Spirogyra chloroplasts are ribbon-shaped and arranged in a spiral. <p>地球上的水以<b>海洋水</b>为主，约占全球总水量的 96.5%。陆地上:
Most of Earth's water is ocean water, about 96.5% of the total. Glaciers, groundwater, lakes and rivers on land, vapour in the air and the water inside living things together make up only about 3.5%.

Fresh water is only about 2.5%, and nearly 70% of it is locked in polar and mountain glaciers. River water, freshwater lakes and shallow groundwater, which people can use easily, are less than 0.3% of all fresh water.

<p>水在<b>固态（冰、雪）</b>、<b>液态（水）</b>、<b>气态（水:
Water keeps changing between solid (ice, snow), liquid (water) and gas (water vapour). These changes of state drive the water cycle.

Water at the sea and lake surface absorbs heat from sunlight and evaporates into vapour. Rising vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets in clouds; where it is colder higher up, it turns straight into ice crystals by deposition. In winter snow falls and builds up in the mountains; in spring and summer snow and glaciers melt and the meltwater flows into rivers.

The sea–land cycle runs between the ocean and the land. It is the most important type of water cycle: it keeps refilling the water on land, so water resources are renewed.

By where they take place, water cycles fall into three types, shown in different colours on the sandbox:

Ocean cycle: seawater evaporates, condenses over the ocean and falls back into it. It moves the largest amount of water.

Sea–land cycle: the cycle between ocean and land, which keeps refilling and renewing water on land.

Land cycle: water on land enters the air by evaporation and plant transpiration, then falls on land again. The basin behind the mountains is an endorheic (interior drainage) region: inland rivers end in an inland lake, and the lake water can only leave by evaporation. This cycle moves the smallest amount of water.

海陆间循环：海洋 ⇄ 陆地，陆地水得到补充: Sea–land cycle: ocean ⇄ land, water on land is replenished
陆地内循环：湖面蒸发、植物蒸腾 → 陆地降水: Land cycle: lake evaporation, plant transpiration → rain on land
三类循环同时进行，共同组成全球水循环: All three cycles run at once and together make up the global water cycle
<p>雨水落到地面后有三条去路：被植被<b>截留</b>后蒸发，<b>下渗</b:
Rain that reaches the ground has three ways to go: it is intercepted by plants and evaporates, it infiltrates into the soil, or it becomes surface runoff. The more that infiltrates, the less runs off and the more groundwater is recharged.

Main factors that affect infiltration:

· Rainfall intensity: the heavier the rain, the more water cannot soak in fast enough
· Slope: the steeper the slope, the faster the water flows and the less soaks in
· Vegetation: roots and leaf litter loosen the soil, so more water soaks in
· Soil texture: sand has large pores and absorbs fast; clay absorbs slowly
· Paved surfaces: concrete and asphalt let almost no water through

The water cycle links the atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and biosphere:

① It keeps the global amount of water in dynamic balance: water evaporated from the ocean returns to it as precipitation and runoff.

② It moves matter and exchanges energy: rivers carry sediment and dissolved substances from land to sea; vapour absorbs heat when it evaporates and releases it when it condenses, carrying heat from low to high latitudes and easing the heat imbalance between latitudes.

③ It shapes the land surface: running water erodes V-shaped valleys upstream and deposits alluvial plains and deltas downstream and at the river mouth.

④ It keeps renewing water resources: fresh water that has been used is replenished by the water cycle.

<p>城市扩张后，农田和绿地变成了建筑、水泥地和沥青路，雨水<b>下渗减少</b:
As a city grows, farmland and green space turn into buildings, concrete and asphalt. Less rain infiltrates, surface runoff increases, and drains carry it quickly into the river:

· flood peaks get higher and arrive earlier, so urban flooding becomes more likely
· groundwater is not recharged and rivers carry less water in the dry season
· less evaporation and transpiration make the city hotter and drier

A sponge city uses permeable paving, green roofs, sunken green space and rain gardens so that it can “soak up, store, filter and purify” water like a sponge, and “release” the stored water when it is needed.

<p>人类活动对水循环影响最大的是<b>地表径流</b>环节，也能影响下渗、蒸发:
Human activity affects surface runoff more than any other process, and can also change infiltration, evaporation and precipitation:

· Building reservoirs: store floodwater and release it in the dry season — cutting flood peaks and topping up low flows; the larger water surface also evaporates more
· Inter-basin water transfer (e.g. China's South-to-North Water Diversion): changes the spatial distribution of surface runoff
· Afforestation: more infiltration and transpiration, less surface runoff and soil erosion
· Over-pumping groundwater: creates a cone of depression in the water table, causes land subsidence and, near the coast, seawater intrusion
· Cloud seeding: spreading catalysts in clouds helps vapour condense and fall as rain
